newsitem.title: UK: Euro bourses end higher after US jobs panic.
newsitem.headline: Euro bourses end higher after US jobs panic.

text.p: European bourses ended with small gains after a volatile afternoon that saw them drop sharply in response to news of strong U.S. jobs growth before staging a recovery, dealers said. The initial drop was sparked by a one-point dive in U.S. Treasury bonds that caught European markets off-guard.
"A lot of bad news had already been priced into the market. Really there were no long positions to be vulnerable to the news," said one British government bond trader.

However, the fall in U.S. bond prices was shortlived, and a firmer trend on Wall Street helped the European markets stabilise. By the time Europe closed the Dow average was up some 45 points at around 5,652.
The U.S. Labor Department said 250,000 non-farm jobs were created during the month, not much different from the consensus figure of 244,000 that economists had forecast on average.
The unemployment rate dropped to 5.1 percent in August, its lowest level in more than seven years, from 5.4 percent in July.
The problem for the markets seemed to lie elsewhere, in a rise in average hourly earnings.

"So if you couple the increase in the payrolls with the increase in wages, it provides fairly strong incentives for the Federal Reserve to step in and raise interest rates," said Hugh Johnson, chief investment officer at First Albany Corp in New York.

"It (the payroll report) is a pretty mixed bag. The bond market was set up for a strong figure and it got it in the hourly earnings average," said David Hewitt, a bond strategist at Tokyo Mitsubishi International in London. Markets had been worrying all week that a strong employment report could prompt the U.S. 9ederal Reserve to raise interest rates at its next policy meeting on September 24.
In London, the FTSE index of leading London shares touched a 1ow of 3,856.8 after the dive in U.S. Treasuries, before closing a net 5.8 points higher at 3,893.0.
In Frankfurt, the DAX IBIS index that tracks all-day electronic trade closed up 10.19 points at 2,542.74.
Paris also dropped at first, but then rallied above 2,000 and closed up 8.52 points at 2,004.75.

The French markets were helped by news of planned income tax cuts plus higher taxes on tobacco and alcohol. The government also predicted that economic growth would rise to 2.3 percent in 1997 from a forecast 1.3 percent this year.
The franc, weak of late due to worries about industrial unrest as the government imposes a tight budget, firmed to 3.4155 per mark from 3.4215 late on Thursday.
The dollar rose modestly during the afternoon and was quoted in late trade at 109.35 yen against 109.10 at the European close on Thursday and at 1.4905 marks versus 1.4850.

"The U.S. data supports the argument for a Fed rate hike this month but probably by only 25 basis points, and the forex market doesn't find this very exciting," said Jonathon Griggs, head of research for treasury products at BZW in London.
Trading in gold was as confused as in other markets after the data, with the price per ounce eventually settling lower at $385.50 after testing support at $385.
CURRENCIES
The dollar was at 1.4905 marks and 109.35 yen, slightly firmer than 1.4850 and 109.10 on Thursday.
STOCK MARKETS
The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares ended up 5.8 points at 3,893.0.
Frankfurt's IBIS DAX index ended up 10.19 points at 2,542.74.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index ended up 8.52 points at 2,004.74.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold closed at $385.50 vs $386.35 on Thursday. Silver was down five cents at $5.15.
